newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria, U.S. firms in $177 mln oil development deal.
newsitem.headline: Algeria, U.S. firms in $177 mln oil development deal.

text.p: U.S.-based oil firms, Anadarko Petroleum Corp and Halliburton Co, on Tuesday signed a $177 million agreement with Algeria's giant oil Sonatrach firm to develop the southern field of Hassi Berkine.

The Algerian state-owned Sonatrach said in a statement sent to Reuters that the deal allows Brown & Root Condor, a joint venture between Sonatrach and Halliburton, to develop a 60,000 barrel per day (bpd) oilfield in Hassi Berkine-Sud.

Sonatrach said the 21-month project was the first stage in a plan to develop the overall Hassi Berkine-Sud field which has a potential of one billion barrels of oil. Other experts estimate the potential at 1.5 billion barrels.
Sonatrach and Anadarko, linked by a production sharing deal, discovered the field in the southeastern basin of Ghadames, in the Sahara, where 34 of Algeria's 207 discoveries lie.
Brown & Root Condor would provide equipment and services to build an array of installations, including reinjection of miscible gas, Sonatrach said.

"The programme comprises, among others, a network pf pipework for five oil wells, one well to inject gas, a train to produce oil with a capacity of 60,000 barrels per day," the Sonatrach statement said.
Sonatrach said Brown & Root Condor would also build a pressurised gas station with a capacity of 2.69 million cubic metres, a pipeline to carry the oil, and a power station.
Sonatrach said Anadarko would fund the project in which six Algerian companies would be associated as subcontractors.
It said 40 percent of the project cost would be in the Algerian dinar local currency.

Sonatrach said it planned a second stage of developing Hassi Berkine-Sud with the building of two additional modules and the generalisation of gas injection in the field, as well as the "setting up a peripheral water injection".
Algeria crude production is expected to surge with the help of several new fields, pushing Algeria oil output to about one million bpd by the year 2000, up from its current OPEC quota of 750,000.

Anadarko, Spanish CEPSA, Italian Agip Spa, Petro-Canada have discovered oil and gas wells in Algeria, mostly since the cash-poor North African country liberalised more its oil and gas legislation in 1991 to attract foreign investors.
